G.Girish, J.

This application is filed under Sections 430 and 528 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita,
2023 for the interim suspension of sentence awarded by the Fast Track Special Court, Palakkad in Sessions Case No.1314/2022.
The applicant is the appellant, who was convicted by the said Court for the commission of offence under Sections 342, 363, 376(AB), 376(2)(f) and 376(2)(k) of the Indian Penal Code.
He was awarded life imprisonment and fine Rs.1,00,000/- under Section 376(AB) and imprisonment for various terms and fine of various amounts for the commission of the other offences.
2. The applicant would contend that his wife has been diagnosed with Cancer requiring prolonged treatment for one year, and there is nobody to take care of her.
For the above reason, the applicant seeks interim suspension of sentence for a period of one month.

3. Annexure-A1 certificate issued by a Medical Officer from Government Medical College, Chest Hospital, Mulankunnathukavu, is relied on by the applicant to substantiate his contentions about the ailment suffered by his wife.

sentences.text: in 4. Heard the learned counsel for the applicant and the learned Senior Public Prosecutor representing the State of Kerala.

5. The learned Senior Public Prosecutor has placed before us the report of the SHO of Police,
Vadakkancherry along with certain medical records pertaining to the treatment for malignancy of a patient by name Rahmath, aged 39 years.
A statement of one Mr.Hakkim, the son of the applicant/appellant, recorded by the above officer, is also placed before us.

In the above statement,
the deponent has stated that the 2nd wife of the applicant is suffering from Cancer and she has been under treatment for the past 10 years, and there is nobody to take care of her.

It is further stated that they are finding it difficult to meet the expenses of the treatment and that it will be a relief if his father is released from the jail for carrying on the treatment of the above said Rahmath.
6.

In the report filed by the S.H.O of Police, Vadakkancherry, the request of the applicant is opposed stating the reason that the suspension of sentence of the above convict would give a wrong message to the public, and that he may commit similar crimes in future.
It is also pointed out that the victim of this case stays near to the house of the applicant.

7. It is evident from the statement of the above said person by name Hakkim, the son of the appellant that the second wife of the in appellant has been undergoing treatment for cancer for the past ten years.

The applicant has been convicted and sentenced by the Trial Court on 21.11.2023 for Xxx vs State Of Kerala on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/82550834/
2 the offence committed during the year 2022.

sentences.text: Thus, it is obvious that the second wife of the applicant was under treatment for Cancer even years prior to the days when the crime involved in this case was committed.
It is to be noted that the offence committed by the applicant is brutal rape perpetrated upon a seven year old girl by subjecting her to criminal intimidation.
The applicant could not have resorted to the above treacherous act, if he had any concern or care for his second wife who had been under treatment for cancer during that time.
When viewed in the above perspective, the bona fides of the reason stated by the applicant about his ardent wish to take care of the treatment of his second wife, appears to be suspicious.

8. It is seen from the records that the Trial Court has relied on the clinching evidence adduced by PW2 - the survivor, PW1 - the mother of the survivor, PW11 - an independent witness and PW13 - the Doctor who examined the survivor, to arrive at the finding that the applicant committed nefarious rape upon a little girl.
We find no reason to think that the Trial Court went wrong in the analysis of the above evidence and arriving at the finding of guilt of the applicant.

in 9. In Preetpal Singh v. State of U.P [(2020) 8 SCC 645] the Apex Court held as follows about the principles governing the grant of bail under section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and the suspension of sentence under section 389 Cr.P.C followed by grant of bail post-conviction:
"36.

entities.text: Preetpal Singh v. State of U.P [(2020) 8 SCC 645]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
There is a difference between grant of bail under S.439 of the CrPC in case of pre - trial arrest and suspension of sentence under S.389 of the CrPC and grant of bail,
post conviction.

In the earlier case there may be presumption of innocence, which is a fundamental postulate of criminal jurisprudence, and the courts may be liberal,
depending on the facts and circumstances of the case, on the principle that bail is the rule and jail is an exception, as held by this Court in Dataram Singh v. State of U.P.
and Anr. (supra).

entities.text:
Dataram Singh v. State of U.P.
and Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, in case of post conviction bail, by suspension of operation of the sentence, there is a finding of guilt and the question of presumption of innocence does not arise.
Nor is the principle of bail being the rule and jail an exception attracted, once there is conviction upon trial.
Rather, the Court considering an application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail, is to consider the prima facie merits of the appeal, coupled with other factors.

There should be strong compelling reasons for grant of bail, notwithstanding an order of conviction, by suspension of sentence, and this strong and compelling in reason must be recorded in the order granting bail, as mandated in S.389(1) of the Cr.P.C."
10.
We find no strong and compelling reason to suspend the sentence of the appellant even for a limited period in view of the aforesaid facts and circumstances of the case.
Needless to say that there is no merit in the present application.
Resultantly, the application stands dismissed.
